subject: Pilot data exchange: staggered testcase licensing & MAP
messages:
From: Evelyn Ochoa <evelyn.ochoa@retailedge.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot data exchange: staged licensing and MAP

Hi Karthik / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — RetailEdge is excited to run a short pilot to validate recommendation quality and safety before we commit to Dedicated. Procurement asked that we put a mutual action plan (MAP) together that covers:

- What evaluation datasets / prompt packs / testcase bundles you will provide
- Staggered licensing (seed -> QA -> acceptance) and timing for each tranche
- Usage constraints (token caps, retention, non-redistribution) and auditability
- Evidence we can present to our security team (access logs, destruction commitments)

Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
1) Deliver a small seed prompt pack (<= 500 testcases) and a larger QA tranche (~3k testcases) with per-tranche access lanes, and
2) Provide an MPA-style draft that explicitly lists allowable uses and takedown/expiry rules?

We attached our initial requirements spreadsheet (RetailEdge_requirements.xlsx). Procurement would like the MAP and a proposed timeline by end of next week so they can circulate.

Thanks,
Evelyn
Evelyn Ochoa
Head of ML Ops, RetailEdge
(attachment: RetailEdge_requirements.xlsx (xlsx))

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Ochoa <evelyn.ochoa@retailedge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot data exchange: staged licensing and MAP

Hi Evelyn — really appreciate the clear ask and the spreadsheet. Short answer: yes, we can support a staggered release and a MAP that lays out explicit use constraints. High-level proposal below; I'll attach a draft MAP for your review this afternoon.

Proposed MAP (high level):
1) Kickoff & inventory (Week 0): agree final list of testcases + labeling guide.
2) Seed tranche (Week 1-2): up to 500 testcases delivered to RetailEdge sandbox; ephemeral credentials, read-only access. Acceptance gate: basic functional smoke tests.
3) QA tranche (Week 3-4): ~3k testcases; expanded sandbox with token caps and KV-cache disabled for evaluation.
4) Acceptance tranche (Week 5): full QA pass + formal acceptance tests; access expires automatically after 30 days unless renewed.
5) Post-acceptance: escrow and destruction clause — Redwood will destroy copies upon request and provide a signed certificate of destruction; audit logs retained for 90 days unless a longer retention is agreed.

Usage constraints we propose including in the MAP: no redistribution, non-derivative use for benchmarking only, token caps per day per seat, and telemetry logs shared to RetailEdge for accountability. We can watermark testcases on access and provide per-request logs.

Attachments: MAP-draft-RetailEdge.pdf (draft, includes redlineable clauses for acceptance gates and destruction).

If that aligns, Ben and I will line up a short MPA review call next week and circulate a redline-friendly version. Proposed lead times: draft MAP by EOD today, 1-hour MPA review on Tue 9/21, seed tranche delivered by 9/24.

Thanks — talk soon.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
(attachment: MAP-draft-RetailEdge.pdf (pdf))

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Ochoa <evelyn.ochoa@retailedge.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 11:02:15 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot data exchange: staged licensing and MAP

Evelyn — a couple of practical notes from ops/legal so the MAP is actionable: 

1) Token/seat caps: we'll include per-tranche daily token caps and a backstop throttle we can enable during QA to protect SLOs.
2) Ephemeral access: seed tranche credentials will be ephemeral keys tied to Vendor Sandbox accounts; keys expire automatically and are rotated.
3) Testcase watermarking / PII: we recommend syntactic watermarking and a short PII scrub checklist; we can supply an anonymized variant set if needed for your legal review.
4) Auditability: request logs and token-level summaries will be shared via a secure drive link; for formal audits we can provide an S3-style log export and a small runbook describing how to verify.

I'll add those as specific clauses in the MAP-draft and flag items Redwood needs redlined (e.g., retention windows and escrow triggers). For timeline: can confirm Ben's proposed schedule from Karthik, but recommend moving the MPA review to Wed 9/22 (gives us time to incorporate RetailEdge's initial redlines).

Also looping Marissa (cc) who will own the dataset ingestion and sandbox provisioning on Redwood's side.

Thanks,
Ben
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Evelyn Ochoa <evelyn.ochoa@retailedge.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot data exchange: staged licensing and MAP

Thanks Karthik/Ben — this is helpful. Procurement reviewed the draft requirements and has two asks before the MPA review: 

- Move the acceptance gate to be deterministic (we need a short acceptance script with pass/fail criteria rather than an ad-hoc QA signoff).
- Add a hard expiry for all seed copies (we prefer 14 days after delivery) and an explicit clause that prevents internal reuse by Redwood for model training.

I've attached our redlines (RE-redlines.docx). Can you incorporate those, and confirm whether Redwood is willing to include the no-training clause for the seed and QA tranches? If so, procurement will be comfortable moving to the 9/24 seed delivery.

Best,
Evelyn
(attachment: RE-redlines.docx (docx))

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Ochoa <evelyn.ochoa@retailedge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2026 16:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot data exchange: staged licensing and MAP

Evelyn — appreciate the specificity. Short answers:

- Deterministic acceptance: yes. We'll add an acceptance script with measurable criteria (precision/recall thresholds on the acceptance corpus, plus performance and safety checks). That will be embedded as an exhibit in the MAP.
- No-training clause: Redwood will agree to a contractual prohibition on using seed and QA tranches for model training or benchmarks outside the scope of the pilot. We'll include carve-outs for aggregate telemetry needed for billing and debug, but nothing that constitutes retention for training.

Next steps:
- Ben to push the updated MAP with your redlines by EOD Fri 9/24.
- Marissa to provision the sandbox and deliver seed tranche on 9/24 morning; credentials will be ephemeral and include the 14-day expiry you requested.
- Quick MPA review call scheduled Wed 9/22 is shifted to Fri 9/24 at 10:00 PT to allow the redline merge. Invite to follow.

I'll also add Laura from Legal (cc) to validate the destruction/escrow language. If all OK after the review call, we can treat delivery as the formal go/no-go trigger for the pilot.

—Karthik
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
